drivingQuestion: Does R' Yehuda exempt even simultaneous striking/cursing, and why?
outcomeNote: Contradiction resolved as two tannaim; reason supplied by R' Chanina

segments.he: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: פָּטוּר בְּבַת אַחַת! תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But isn’t it taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Yehuda says: He is exempt» even if he struck or cursed them «simultaneously?» The Gemara answers: These are the opinions of «two tanna’im,» and they each expressed their opinion «in accordance with» that «of Rabbi Yehuda.»

segments.he: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּפָטַר? אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: נֶאֶמְרָה בְּרָכָה לְמַטָּה, וְנֶאֶמְרָה בְּרָכָה לְמַעְלָה. מָה לְמַעְלָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שׁוּתָּפוּת — אַף לְמַטָּה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שׁוּתָּפוּת. וְאִיתַּקַּשׁ הַכָּאָה לִקְלָלָה.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What is the reasoning of the one who exempts» the son from punishment? «Rabbi Ḥanina said: Blessing is stated below» (Leviticus 20:9), with regard to cursing parents, «and blessing is stated above» (Exodus 22:27), with regard to cursing God. The Sages used the word blessing as a euphemism for cursing, as it was their custom to avoid uncouth language. «Just as» the statement «above,» in Exodus, is referring to a curse «that does not involve partnership,» as God is One, «so too» the statement «below,» in Leviticus, is referring exclusively to a curse of a parent «that does not involve partnership,» i.e., when there is no doubt with regard to his identity. «And striking is juxtaposed with cursing.» Just as one is not liable for cursing when it is unclear who his father is, the same applies to striking.
